newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal sector to begin wage overhaul talks.
newsitem.headline: German metal sector to begin wage overhaul talks.

text.p: Germany's huge metal and engineering sector, employing some four million workers in industries from car-making to electronics, were on Wednesday due to begin talks aimed at reforming the wage bargaining system that has served it from the 1950s.

Negotiators for the Gesamtmetall employers federation and IG Metall, Germany's largest trade union, are expected to explore a range of options including plans for early retirement schemes and the creation of more flexible working practices.

Neither side would say what the first set of discussions, to be held in Frankfurt amid increasing unemployment in the sector and discontent from firms at the current bargaining system, would focus on.

But union officials are hoping that talks will return to a model they have already proposed that would allow workers effectively to retire five years early while retaining their full pension entitlements.

Under the proposed model, 55-year-old workers would receive 85 percent of their full salary for the last 10 years of their working life. They would then work full-time for five years before being released at the age of 60.
Under the scheme, which IG Metall says has the support of the Bonn government, pension contributions would continue to be paid in full for the last 10 years.

Employers are meanwhile seeking to have exemption clauses built in to collective wage agreements that would, for example, more easily allow companies to save costs by operating at reduced capacity when business was turning down.
